summary: 玩偶曾用于宗教仪式，也陪伴儿童游戏。木、蜡、瓷、布、赛璐珞和塑料等材料的更替，改变了玩偶的外观、可动性及批量生产方式，传统手艺则延续至今。
logic: 古代墓葬与祭祀中的玩偶
欧洲木、蜡及瓷偶的演变
塑料普及和传统手作并存

paragraphs.brief: 早期的娃娃往往描写宗教人物，或用作玩物，可能是用泥土、毛皮或木材等原始材料制造的。
sentences: What is today a simple children’s toy has a surprisingly rich history.
今天的简单儿童玩具有着令人惊讶的丰富历史。
Dolls have been a part of humankind for thousands of years.
几千年来，洋娃娃一直是人类的一部分。
Often depicting religious figures, or used as playthings, early dolls were probably made from primitive materials such as clay, fur, or wood.
早期的娃娃往往描写宗教人物，或用作玩物，可能是用泥土、毛皮或木材等原始材料制造的。

paragraphs.brief: 由平板木制成、用各种设计以及用粘土制成的 " 头发 " 制成的木偶往往在2000年公元前的埃及坟墓中被发现。
sentences: Dolls constructed of flat pieces of wood, painted with various designs, and with ‘hair’ made of clay, have often been found in Egyptian graves dating back to 2000 BC.
由平板木制成、用各种设计以及用粘土制成的 " 头发 " 制成的木偶往往在2000年公元前的埃及坟墓中被发现。
Egyptian tombs of wealthy families have included pottery dolls.
埃及富裕家庭的坟墓包括陶瓷娃娃。
Dolls being placed in these graves leads some to believe that they were cherished possessions.
被埋在这些坟墓里的人相信他们是珍爱的财产

paragraphs.brief: 来自古希腊和罗马的女孩向女神献上木偶之后她们太"成熟" 无法玩娃娃。
sentences: Girls from ancient Greece and Rome offered their wooden dolls to goddesses after they were too ‘grown-up’ to play with dolls.
来自古希腊和罗马的女孩向女神献上木偶之后她们太"成熟" 无法玩娃娃。
Most ancient dolls that were found in tombs were very simple creations, often made from such materials as clay, rags, wood, or bone.
在坟墓中发现的大多数古代娃娃都是非常简单的创造物，往往是用粘土、抹布、木材或骨头等材料制造的。
Some of the more unique dolls were made with ivory or wax.
一些更独特的娃娃是用象牙或蜡做的。
The main goal was to make the doll as lifelike as possible.
主要目标是让娃娃尽可能像生命一样。
That ideal led to the creation of dolls with movable limbs and removable garments, dating back to 600 BC.
这一理想导致了可移动肢体和可移动服装的娃娃的产生，可追溯到公元前600年。

paragraphs.brief: 在古代洋娃娃时代之后，欧洲成为了洋娃娃生产的主要枢纽。
sentences: Following the era of the ancient dolls, Europe became a major hub for doll production.
在古代洋娃娃时代之后，欧洲成为了洋娃娃生产的主要枢纽。
These dolls were primarily made of wood.
这些娃娃主要是木制的
Fewer than 30 examples of primitive wooden stump dolls from England survive today.
不到30个英国原始木质娃娃今天存活下来。
The Grodnertal area of Germany produced many peg wooden dolls, a type of doll that has very simple peg joints and resembles a clothespin (a device for hanging washing on a clothesline).
德国的格罗德纳塔尔地区生产了许多木偶，这种娃娃有很简单的钉接节，类似于衣物皮(一个在衣物线上挂上洗衣服的装置)。
An alternative to wood was developed in the 1800s.
1800年代开发了木材的替代品。

paragraphs.brief: " 组合 " 是指用于制造娃娃头和人体的雕塑木或纸的混合物。
sentences: ‘Composition’ is a collective term for mixtures of pulped wood or paper that were used to make doll heads and bodies.
" 组合 " 是指用于制造娃娃头和人体的雕塑木或纸的混合物。
These mixtures were moulded under pressure, creating a durable doll that could be mass-produced.
这些混合物是在压力下制成的，产生一个可大规模生产的耐久娃娃。
Manufacturers closely guarded the recipes for their mixtures, sometimes using strange ingredients like ash or eggshells.
制造商严格保管其混合物的配方，有时使用奇怪的成分，如灰或蛋壳。
Papier-mâché, a type of composition, was one of the most popular mixtures.
Papier-mâché是一种最受欢迎的混合物。

paragraphs.brief: 除了木偶外，蜡娃娃在17世纪和18世纪越来越受欢迎。
sentences: In addition to wooden dolls, wax dolls grew in popularity in the 17th and 18th centuries.
除了木偶外，蜡娃娃在17世纪和18世纪越来越受欢迎。
Munich in Germany was a major manufacturing centre for wax dolls.
德国的慕尼黑是蜡娃娃的主要制造中心。
Wax dollmakers would model a doll’s head in wax or clay, and then cover it with plaster to create a mould.
瓦克斯娃娃制造商会用蜡或粘土来模拟娃娃的头部，然后用石膏盖上，以制造一个模具。
Then they would pour melted wax into the cast.
然后他们就会把融化的蜡倒进石膏里
The wax for the head would be very thin, no more than 3 mm.
头部的蜡会非常薄，不超过3毫米。
Some of the most distinctive wax dolls were created in England between 1850 and 1930.
1850年至1930年期间，英国制造了一些最独特的蜡娃娃。
One of the first dolls that portrayed a baby was made in England from wax at the beginning of the 19th century.
最早描绘婴儿的娃娃之一是19世纪初在英国用蜡做的

paragraphs.brief: Porcelain一般用于指瓷娃娃和饼干娃娃；瓷器是玻璃，而饼干是胶。
sentences: Around the same time, porcelain became popular.
大约在同一时间，瓷器变得流行。
It is made by firing special clays in a kiln at more than 2372 degrees Fahrenheit (1300°C), and only a few clays can withstand firing at such high temperatures.
其制造方法是在法赫伦海拔(13,00°C)超过2372度的窑炉中发射特殊粘土，只有少量粘土能够承受如此高的温度的燃烧。
Porcelain is used generically to refer to both china and bisque dolls; china is glazed, whereas bisque is unglazed.
Porcelain一般用于指瓷娃娃和饼干娃娃；瓷器是玻璃，而饼干是胶。
Germany, France, and Denmark started creating china heads for dolls in the 1840s.
德国、法国和丹麦开始在1840年代创造中国人头
These china heads were replaced in the 1860s by ones made of bisque.
这些中国人的头在1860年代被饼干取代了
Bisque, which is porcelain fired twice with colour added to it after the first firing, looked more like skin than china did.
在第一次射击后又发射了两次彩色的瓷砖，比瓷器更像皮肤。

paragraphs.brief: 在法国，贝贝在1880年代很受欢迎，今天它已成为一个非常受欢迎的娃娃。
sentences: In France, the bébé was popular in the 1880s, and it has become a highly sought-after doll today.
在法国，贝贝在1880年代很受欢迎，今天它已成为一个非常受欢迎的娃娃。
The bébé, first made in the 1850s, was different from its predecessors because it depicted a younger girl.
贝贝是1850年代首次制作的，与以前的版本不同，因为它描绘了一个较年轻的女孩。
Until then, most French dolls were representations of adults.
在那之前，大多数法国娃娃都是成年人的表情。
Although the French dolls were unrivalled in their artistry, German bisque dolls became quite popular because they were not as expensive.
虽然法国娃娃在艺术界是无比的，但德国饼干娃娃却变得相当流行，因为它们不那么昂贵。
Kammer & Reinhardt introduced a bisque character doll in the 1900s, starting a trend of creating realistic dolls.
Kammer & Reinhardt在1900年代推出了一个双曲字符娃娃，开始出现创造现实娃娃的趋势。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然不像其他材料制作的娃娃那么精密，但布娃娃还是很受人喜爱，往往就像孩子的第一个玩具。
sentences: For many centuries, rag dolls were made by mothers for their children.
许多世纪以来，母亲为其子女制造了布娃娃。
The term ‘rag doll’ refers generically to dolls made of any fabric.
“拉格娃娃”一词一般是指用任何布料制成的娃娃。
‘Cloth doll’ refers to a subset of rag dolls made of linen or cotton.
”Cloth娃娃”是指用床单或棉制成的布娃娃。
Commercially produced rag dolls were first introduced in the 1850s by English and American manufacturers.
1850年代，英国和美国制造商首次推出商业生产的布娃娃。
Although not as sophisticated as dolls made from other materials, rag dolls were well loved, often as a child’s first toy.
虽然不像其他材料制作的娃娃那么精密，但布娃娃还是很受人喜爱，往往就像孩子的第一个玩具。

paragraphs.brief: 娃娃生产集中在美国新英格兰地区，用皮革、橡胶、皮革和布料等各种材料制成娃娃。
sentences: Dollmaking did not become an industry in the United States until after the Civil War in the 1860s.
直到1860年代的内战之后，制货业才成为美国的工业。
Doll production was concentrated in the New England region of the United States, with dolls made from a variety of materials such as leather, rubber, papier-mâché, and cloth.
娃娃生产集中在美国新英格兰地区，用皮革、橡胶、皮革和布料等各种材料制成娃娃。
Celluloid was developed in the state of New Jersey in the late 1860s and was used to manufacture dolls until the mid-1950s.
新泽西州在1860年代后期开发了细胞素，并一直用于制造洋娃娃，直至1950年代中期。
German, French, American, and Japanese factories churned out cheaply produced celluloid dolls in mass quantities.
德国、法国、美国和日本的工厂大量抛出廉价生产的纤维素娃娃。
However, celluloid fell out of favour because of its extreme flammability and propensity to fade in bright light.
然而，由于纤维素极易燃，而且极易在明亮的光线下消退，因此细胞素失去了优势。
After World War I, dollmakers experimented with plastics.
第一次世界大战后，娃娃制造商实验塑料。
Hard plastic dolls were manufactured in the 1940s.
1940年代制造了硬塑料娃娃。
They resembled composition dolls, but they were much more durable.
它们像布料娃娃，但更耐久
Other materials used in doll manufacturing included rubber, foam rubber, and vinyl in the 1950s and 1960s.
洋娃娃制造中使用的其他材料包括1950年代和1960年代的橡胶、泡沫橡胶和乙烯基。
Vinyl changed dollmaking, allowing dollmakers to root hair into the head, rather than using wigs or painting the hair.
维尼尔改变了娃娃制作，允许娃娃制造者把头发扎在头上，而不是用假发或画头发。
Although most dolls are now mass-manufactured using these modern materials, many modern dollmakers are still using the traditional materials of the past to make collectible dolls.
虽然现在大多数娃娃都是使用这些现代材料制造的，但许多现代娃娃制造商仍在利用过去的传统材料来制造可收集的娃娃。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Bisque dolls appear less realistic than dolls made of china.
items.zh: 饼干娃娃看起来不像瓷器做的娃娃那么现实
items.why: 原文说 bisque 更像皮肤，即更逼真。题干说“更不逼真 ",与原文相反，故 FALSE。关键词映射 : appearrealistic = /ookead more like skin。

items.en: French dolls tended to cost more than German bisque dolls.
items.zh: 法国娃娃的成本往往比德国饼干娃娃还要高。
items.why: 德国的“不那么贵” =” 相比之下法国更贵。等价转述为题干，故 TRUE。

items.en: The first rag dolls were made in the 1850s.
items.zh: 第一批布娃娃是1850年代制造的
items.why: 1850s 指商业化生产的开始，而非布偶本身首次出现。布偶“几百年来" 就有，故题干错误为 FALSE。

items.en: Only dolls made of cotton or linen are classified as cloth dolls.
items.zh: 只有用棉花或亚麻做的娃娃才被归类为布娃娃。
items.why: 定义里明确: cloth doll = 用 linen/cotton 的子集二“只有棉或亚麻”才算 cloth dolls,故 TRUE。易错点: 不要把 rag dolls (任何布料) 混同为 cloth dolls。

items.en: Dolls made of celluloid tended to lose their colour.
items.zh: 由纤维素制成的圆圆形往往会失去颜色。
items.why: 赛璐珞在强光下容易褪色，印证这种娃娃容易失去原有颜色。

items.en: Composition dolls lasted longer than the plastic dolls that were made in the 1940s.
items.zh: 构成娃娃持续的时间比1940年代制造的塑料娃娃要长。
items.why: 四十年代的硬塑料娃娃外形似混合材料娃娃，却耐用得多，题干颠倒了比较双方。

items.en: Doll collectors prefer a doll to be dressed in its original clothing.
items.zh: 玩偶收藏家更喜欢一个洋娃娃穿着它原来的衣服。
items.why: 文章说收藏级娃娃仍会使用传统材料，没有说明收藏者对原装服饰有何偏好。

pairs: that could be put in different positions
能够摆成不同姿势／可活动的
